ORAL ORDER 1.

Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr.Jal Unwala with learned advocate Mr.Vijay Limbachiya appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr.J.K.Shah appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.

1.1. While learned APP Mr.Shah would inform that charge- sheet is filed during the pendency of the present application, since the matter has already opened, this Court has deemed it appropriate to take up the present application.
2. Rule. Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State.

The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.
11993007250022/2025 registered with Gandhidham B-Division Police Station, Kuchchh East - Gandhidham for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 114 of the IPC.

entities.text: Gandhidham B-Division Police Station, Kuchchh East - Gandhidham
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/2182/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined application may be dismissed.
6.
I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.

Following aspects are considered:-
i. The allegation being that the accused had committed offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC.

ii. The fact that the present appears to be a commercial transaction, more particularly, the FIR itself narrating that the present applicant and the complainant party were doing business with each other since around 7 years.

iii. It would also appear that the allegation being that the applicant,
though having purchased goods worth Rs.4,93,00,000/- having paid part of the amount, had not paid an amount of Rs.2,00,91,814/-.
iv. It would also appear in this regard that the transaction is for a period between 01.04.2022 to 01.04.2024.

v. Considering such a position, it would prima facie appear that the present is a continuing regular commercial transaction between the parties and whereas, since it appears that the present applicant has paid more than half NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/2182/2026 ORDER DATED: 03/03/2026 undefined of the amount to the complainant - party, allegation for offence punishable under Section 420 may not lie.
vi. It also appears that the present applicant is in custody since 06.01.2026 and as noticed hereinabove charge-sheet is filed and the applicant has no other antecedent.

This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
7.

prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
